newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TIMELINES - Today in History - April 14.
newsitem.headline: TIMELINES - Today in History - April 14.

text.p: **BIRTHDAYS*
Australian archaeologist VERE GORDON CHILDE, who claimed people should suicide when they reached a certain age (and did so by jumping from Govett's Leap in the Blue Mountains), was born in 1892.
British actor SIR JOHN GIELGUD was born in 1904.
American actor ROD STEIGER, who won an Oscar for "In The Heat Of The Night", was born in 1925.
U.S. country singer LORETTA LYNN was born in 1935. She had about 80 hits in the country charts between 1960 and 1980. Her autobiography "Coalminer's Daughter" became a film.
Australian ballet dancer GARTH WELCH, who became a principal dancer with MARILYN JONES, was born in 1936.
Politician RALPH WILLIS (1994 Federal Treasurer) was born in Melbourne in 1938.
British actress JULIE CHRISTIE was born in 1940.
Uunited Kingdom keyboard player with "Hot Chocolate", LARRY FERGUSON, was born in 1948.
**EVENTS**
1759: GEORGE FREDERICK HANDEL, the German composer who became a British subject in 1726, died in London.
1772: Miss ELIZABETH RUSSEL of Streatham in England was
buried at the ripe old age of 104.
Neighbours had never seen her in anything but skirts, and were surprised to learn at her death, that Miss ELIZABETH was a man!
1865: United States President ABRAHAM LINCOLN (16th U.S President) was assassinated at Ford's Theatre in Washington, while attending a performance of "Our American Cousin".
He was shot in the back of the head by JOHN WILKES BOOTH.
LINCOLN ended slavery in 1863 with the Emancipation Declaration.
1903: The typhus vaccine was discovered by Doctor HARRY PLOTZ in New York.
1912: The "unsinkable" TITANIC hit an iceberg and sank off the Grand Banks of Newfoundland on its first voyage with the loss of 1,513 lives.
The wreck was located by a robot submarine in 1985, four kilometres down in an ocean canyon. Salvage operations began in 1987.

Fourteen years before the tragedy, MORGAN ROBERTSON wrote a novel called "The Wreck Of The Titan", about the maiden voyage of a luxury liner that struck an iceberg on a foggy April night. It may have been a coincidence, but the ship in ROBERTSON's novel had far too few lifeboats to save all the passengers, the same situation that occured 14 years later on the TITANIC.
1933: LORES BONNEY (the cousin of aviator BERT HINKLER) took off from Darwin in a Gypsy Moth to become the first woman to fly from Australia to England.
Her record-breaking flight took 68 days.
1954: Soviet diplomat VLADIMIR PETROV sought politicial asylum in Australia.
1956: The first video tape was demonstrated in Chicago.
1983: The first cordless telephone was introduced in Britain.
1987: Soviet President MIKHAIL GORBACHEV "wrong-footed" the White House by proposing a round of arms reductions.
He offered to remove the entire stock of Soviet short-range missiles in Europe, and sought an early disarmament treaty with the United States.
